item.description:
Ranking

Went to rush school project, as long as I can get into AIS3 it’s fine

Welcome

  • Number of solvers：386/389
  • Author：Curious

If you copy directly it will beA I S 3 { T h i s _ I s _ J u s t _ A _ F a k e _ F l a g _ ~ ~ }
But
Typing it out character by character works fine.

FLAG：AIS3{Welcome_And_Enjoy_The_CTF_!}

Ramen CTF

  • Number of solvers：329/389
  • Author：Whale120

On the top right of the receipt you can see the Unified Business Number, so you can reverse lookup the company name from it.

Since a UBN has 8 digits, but the photo only shows 7, brute-forcing the last digit reveals the UBN is 34785923.

Finally, scanning the QR code on the ramen item gives the result：蝦拉麵

FLAG：AIS3{樂山溫泉拉麵:蝦拉麵}

Login Screen 1

  • Number of solvers：217/389
  • Author：Ching367436

At first, logging in with the provided guest/guest/000000 shows that admin is required.

When trying admin/admin, the 2FA code is unknown.
Looking at the source code in init.php, we find user.db.

1
2

// Database setup
$db = new SQLite3('users.db'); // Create a new SQLite3 database
// Create the users and posts tables if they don't exist
$db->exec("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Users (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password TEXT NOT NULL,
    code TEXT NOT NULL
)");

So http://login-screen.ctftime.uk:36368/users.db can be downloaded.
Opening with Notepad reveals the 2FA code:51756447753485459839

web flag checker

  • Number of solvers：138/389
  • Author：Chumy

See this .wasm in F12. So http://chals1.ais3.org:29998/index.wasm Download this

Find a website that converts to .wat https://webassembly.github.io/wabt/demo/wasm2wat/ I uploaded the file.
The program saw a block called flagchecker (it’s a bit long, so I’m not including the ).
There were some variable declarations inside.

def ror(val, shift, width=64):
    return ((val >> shift) | (val << (width - shift))) & ((1 << width) - 1)

expected = [
    7577352992956835434,
    7148661717033493303,
    -7081446828746089091 % (1 << 64),
    -7479441386887439825 % (1 << 64),
    8046961146294847270,
]

# 根據程式碼的推算，shift 是從這個常數得來的：
magic = -39934163 & 0xFFFFFFFF
shifts = [(magic >> (i * 6)) & 0x3F for i in range(5)]

# 還原 flag
flag_bytes = b""
for const, shift in zip(expected, shifts):
    chunk = ror(const, shift).to_bytes(8, "little")
    flag_bytes += chunk

print(flag_bytes.decode())

FLAG：AIS3{W4SM_R3v3rsing_w17h_g0_4pp_39229dd}

Stream

  • Number of Solvers：146/389
  • Author：Whale120

According to the code,

1

print(hexor(flag, getrandbits(256)))

That is, C = flag XOR (k ** 2)
Since XOR is reversible, we can use the beginning of FLAG, AIS3{, to work backwards.

AIS3{’s ASCII code is 41 49 53 33 7B
Convert it to bytes, and then see which segment, starting from the 25th byte from the end (because flag is about 25 bytes long), can be XORed with the characters AIS3{ to calculate the bytes corresponding to k**2.
For example:

1
2

c_byte[i] = flag_byte[i] XOR k_squared_byte[i]
=> k_squared_byte[i] = c_byte[i] XOR flag_byte[i]

This allows us to deduce the contents of k_squared over several bytes.
Then convert it to bytes and check if it matches the leading AIS3{

import math

# 已知的旗標前綴和後綴
prefix = b"AIS3{"
suffix = b"}"

with open("output.txt", "r") as f:
    lines = f.read().splitlines()
cipher_hex = lines[-1].strip()
cipher_int = int(cipher_hex, 16)

flag_found = None
key_int = None

for L in range(6, 50):
    if L < len(prefix) or L < len(suffix):
        continue  
    X = cipher_int & ((1 << (8 * L)) - 1)     
    H = cipher_int >> (8 * L)                
    # 計算可能的k值範圍
    lower_bound = H << (8 * L)
    upper_bound = (H << (8 * L)) + ((1 << (8 * L)) - 1)
    k_min = math.isqrt(lower_bound)    
    if k_min * k_min < lower_bound:
        k_min += 1
    k_max = math.isqrt(upper_bound) 
    if k_min > k_max:
        continue
    for k in range(k_min, k_max + 1):
        k_square = k * k
        if not (lower_bound <= k_square <= upper_bound):
            continue
        plaintext_int = cipher_int ^ k_square
        plaintext_bytes = plaintext_int.to_bytes(L, 'big')
        if plaintext_bytes.startswith(prefix) and plaintext_bytes.endswith(suffix):
            flag_found = plaintext_bytes
            key_int = k
            break
    if flag_found:
        break

print("FLAG:",flag_found.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))

FLAG：AIS3{no_more_junks...plz}

Random_RSA

  • Number of Solvers：83/389
  • Author：hahabox0

The question mentions using LCG to generate p and q.

1

rng = lambda x: (a*x + b) % m

Then, run rng() from seed until it hits a prime number, which is used as p. Then, run rng() again from p, finding the next prime number and using it as q.
The question gives three consecutive LCG outputs, so we can infer a and b.

1
2
3

h0 = rng(seed)
h1 = rng(h0)
h2 = rng(h1)

According to the LCG formula,

  • h1 = a*h0+b mod m
  • h2 = a*h1+b mod m

Algebraic derivation yields

# 定義迭代 FGSM 攻擊函數
@tf.function
def i_fgsm_attack(image, label, epsilon, num_iterations, alpha):
    image = tf.convert_to_tensor(image)
    adv_image = tf.identity(image)
    for _ in range(num_iterations):
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            tape.watch(adv_image)
            prediction = model(adv_image)
            target = tf.one_hot(label, 1000)
            loss = -tf.keras.losses.categorical_crossentropy(target, prediction)
        gradient = tape.gradient(loss, adv_image)
        signed_grad = tf.sign(gradient)
        adv_image = adv_image + alpha * signed_grad
        adv_image = tf.clip_by_value(adv_image, image - epsilon, image + epsilon)
        adv_image = tf.clip_by_value(adv_image, -1, 1)  # 確保在預處理後的範圍內
    return adv_image
